function: Cascaded BS-RIS-UE channel feedback: AE1 compresses the full channel once per large timescale; AE2 compresses its per-RIS-unit variation ratio vector in the next T intervals (pp. 2-3).
system: FDD, BS with 32-antenna ULA, 16x16 passive reflecting RIS (UPA), single-antenna UE, direct link blocked; 2.655 GHz (pp. 2, 4).
method: Two autoencoders trained with MSE and Adam: convolutional AE1 with RefineNet blocks and fully connected AE2 with residual decoder, 4-bit quantization; unsupervised reconstruction, paradigm not named (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: BS-RIS CSI from Saleh-Valenzuela model with AR time variation (rho=0.9); RIS-UE CSI from Wireless Insite; 200,000 samples split 8:1:1 into training, validation, test (p. 4).
test_conditions: Same dataset for training and test (8:1:1 split); UE at random positions in 30 m x 40 m, 1 m/s; T=4 and 9, compression ratios varied (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Learned: baseline [11], Quan-transformer feedback simplified to AE1, always feeding back the full cascaded channel. Non-learned: RVQ codebook-based feedback (footnote 3) (p. 4).
metrics: NMSE versus equivalent feedback overhead in bits; FLOPs and inference time (pp. 4-5).
complexity: FLOPs in Fig. 5; proposed about 1/(T+1) of baseline; inference time AE1 0.214 ms GPU, 3.354 ms CPU; AE2 0.067 ms GPU, 0.102 ms CPU (p. 5).
openness: none; no code or data link, channels generated by the authors (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 4: "We use the Saleh-Valenzuela channel model to generate BS-RIS CSI samples [19] and Wireless Insite to generate RIS-UE CSI samples [20]." Textbook model plus the authors' own scene; no 3GPP TR 38.901, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 4: "The dataset is divided into training, validation, and test sets in an 8:1:1 ratio." Test data are a held-out part of the same data; T, compression ratio and codeword length are sweeps, with no scenario, band or configuration unseen in training.
q3_support: p. 4: "For comparison purposes, we consider [11] as a baseline." (earlier learned cascaded-channel feedback, simplified to AE1); footnote 3, p. 4: "We also consider the typical RVQ codebook-based feedback method as a baseline" and "The NMSE performance is higher than 0 dB even when using 480 bits for feedback" (non-learned).
q4_support: p. 5: "the inference times for AE1 and AE2 are 0.214 ms and 0.067 ms" on GPU, and "The Floating Point Operations (FLOPs) for the two different methods" are plotted in Fig. 5.
q5_support: p. 4: "A total of 200,000 different cascaded channel samples are generated." The data are generated by the authors; no code or data link is given and no public dataset or measurement is used.
notes: A letter, eligible. Area 2: cascaded channel feedback with MSE autoencoders; channel estimation is assumed perfect (p. 2, footnote 2). q1: the BS-RIS channel is Saleh-Valenzuela and the RIS-UE channel comes from Wireless Insite on the authors' own scene, so not met; reviewer to confirm that it is not a shared dataset. q3: the learned baseline is ref. [11] simplified by the authors to AE1, and the RVQ codebook baseline appears only in footnote 3 with no curve; reviewer to confirm.
